image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small-format Makro wholesale store building, detailed front elevation with a wide glazed entrance under a deep blue fascia banner carrying the red makro wordmark, profiled steel cladding across the upper front and a slim entrance canopy, plain profiled steel side and rear walls with a roller service shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: blue profiled steel sheeting and printed banner vinyl at the front, plate glass entrance, plain unpainted profiled steel on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Makro / CP Axtra. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92, up from 0.82. 3408/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. Draw calls remain the binding axis. On the brief: the elevation stack now matches the rectified plate (1.10 m of ribbed blue over the banner, the glazing 1.56 m tall), the shutter has a thin light frame and a slatted galvanised face at its measured position, and the rooftop plant is three louvred twin-fan condensers down the -X side plus two hooded ducted units on the +X half. Residuals: half-round hoods for the plate's quarter-round elbows, no lit interior behind the glass, ribs as a tile with no corner silhouette.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m (bounds +-4.00, 0..4.97, -3.52..3.50): canopy nose on the declared front face, coping ring at one level all round, three condensers and two ducted units standing above it to 4.97 (8% on one axis, inside the 10% tolerance). Meshy agrees on height to 0.7%. Front stack measured off the rectified plate: coping 4.50..4.60, blue band 3.40..4.50, banner 2.34..3.38, canopy 2.10..2.28 with its lip to 1.86, glazing 0.22..1.78, plinth 0..0.21.
featureReviews.notes: Second build. The first had the glazing 2.4 m tall and 0.5 m of cladding over the banner, which read as a squat box with no room above the sign; the plant sat along the front parapet. Residual: the plate's building is nearer 6.6 m deep than the shared module's 7.0.

featureReviews.evidence: Banner x -3.65..+3.65, y 2.34..3.38, navy #283773 (crop sd 1), 6 cm proud of the blue cladding. The face is the plate's OWN rectified banner crop (1099 x 156 -> 2048 x 294 atlas band), so the red lowercase makro with its pale keyline is the real letterform at the real position (x -1.39..+1.67) with the plate's weathering.
featureReviews.notes: Residual: the crop is a 1.9x upscale of a 1024 plate, so the keyline is soft at high zoom.

featureReviews.evidence: Blue profiled steel #3a5f92 (plate #335175 across the ribs) as a 1.10 m band above the banner, full-height pilasters at x -3.97..-2.97 and 3.40..3.97 with 5 cm corner returns, and the canopy lip; white profiled steel #d8dbde on the ring, sides and rear. Both carry the same baked 8-rib tile at 0.88 m (0.11 m pitch, the mean of the 0.117 front / 0.100 side measurements), world-planar so the ribs run vertical on every wall.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's cladding was flat colour. Residual: the ribs are a tile, so they have no silhouette at the corners.

featureReviews.evidence: Glazing x -3.00..3.40 x y 0.22..1.78 as pale tinted plate #8f9a9a at opacity 0.92 over a mid-grey backdrop slab (0x6a6e72) folded into the deck submission; light aluminium jambs, head, sill, transom at 1.50 and nine mullions at -2.31 -1.61 -0.90 -0.33 0.24 0.79 1.35 2.05 2.75, the three narrow bays being the door leaves over a kick rail. Concrete canopy 2.10..2.28 cantilevering to z 3.46 under a blue lip 1.86..2.14 at 3.50. Turntable gate runs without --allow-holes.
featureReviews.notes: Residual: the plate shows a lit sales floor through the glass; an exterior shell does not.

featureReviews.evidence: +X elevation rectified off the plate: shutter opening 0.60 m back from the front corner, 1.95 m wide, 2.25 m tall -> z 0.05..2.00 against the template's shell face at 2.50. 36 galvanised slats of alternating thickness at 0.0625 m pitch (plate: 0.06) under the spangle tile, a 0.06 m light aluminium guide rail each side (plate: ~0.05) and a 0.14 m head box.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's shutter wore a 0.3 m frame and a flat grey face. Not mirrored onto -X.

featureReviews.evidence: Roof rectified top-down: three twin-fan condensers (1.05 x 0.68 x 1.40 casing, lid flange, two dark fan discs under light guard rings and bars, eight-blade louvres over dark back plates on the +X and +Z faces, seam, rails, conduit box) as ONE instanced geometry with per-part vertex tones, in a row down the -X side at z -2.05 / -0.40 / 1.25; two 2.1 m ducted units along X on the +X half with a rounded hood each, and a low duct run at the rear, merged with the shutter. All galvanised under the baked spangle tile, standing above the coping.
featureReviews.notes: The first build strung three plain boxes along the front parapet. Residual: the plate's hoods are quarter-round elbows; these are half-round.

name: Makro Store Building
notes: Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. A real Makro is an order of magnitude larger than this; scaled down to the shared module at the user's direction, so it reads as a brand-liveried small-format store rather than the real warehouse.
